events.content:
The dashboard now pre-renders a useful shell: its heading and placeholders for the cards, chart, and invoices appear while the data request runs. The request sits inside a Suspense boundary in [app/page.tsx](/workspace/app/page.tsx:59), and [next.config.ts](/workspace/next.config.ts:3) enables Partial Prefetching.

`npm run build` passed. I also checked the generated HTML: it contains the dashboard heading and section placeholders instead of only the route loading indicator.

The dashboard data still depends on the existing `api.example.com` endpoint, so I could verify the shell but not a successful live data response.

The request sits inside a Suspense boundary in [app/page.tsx](/workspace/app/page.tsx:59), and [next.config.ts](/workspace/next.config.ts:3) enables Partial Prefetching.

`npm run build` passed. I also checked the generated HTML: it contains the dashboard heading and section placeholders instead of only the route loading indicator.

The dashboard data still depends on the existing `api.example.com` endpoint, so I could verify the shell but not a successful live data response.

shellCommands.command: /bin/bash -lc 'git status --short && git log -1 --oneline && rg -n "Suspense|connection|cookies|headers|fetch|use cache|dynamic|ppr|loading" app next.config.ts package.json'
/bin/bash -lc 'for f in app/*.tsx; do echo "$f"; cat "$f"; done'
/bin/bash -lc 'git diff -- app/page.tsx next.config.ts tsconfig.json && git status --short'

/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
html = Path('.next/server/app/index.html').read_text()
shell = html.split('<script>requestAnimationFrame', 1)[0]
for label in ['Dashboard', 'Total Revenue', 'Total Invoices', 'Revenue', 'Latest Invoices', 'Loading dashboard...']:
    print(f'{label}: {label in shell}')
print(shell[shell.index('<body>'):][-1100:])
PY"
